k: "Whoever had assumed ihram for Hajj, or for Hajj and Umrah together, did not finish the ihram till the Day of Sacrifice." No cutting until after the stoning on the {1}th. (Hanbalis recommend that one who has no hady with him change his ihram to an Umrah on arrival — he then becomes a Tamattu' pilgrim.)
"Whoever has the hady with him should assume ihram for Hajj along with Umrah, and should not finish the ihram till he finishes both." Qiran also owes a hady.
"Whoever joins Umrah to Hajj must offer what hady is easy" (Quran {1}) — Tamattu' and Qiran. Ifrad owes none.

"Whoever performs Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals… This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram." Qiran counts as joining the two, so it owes a hady too; Ifrad owes none. Who counts as a resident differs a little between the schools.
"…and the people of Makkah from Makkah." The companions who had done Umrah entered ihram for Hajj as they set out for Mina — no trip to a miqat is needed.
"…as the day his mother bore him" — free of sins, as if born anew.
"…except the menstruating women, who were excused." Safiyyah (RA) could leave because she had already done tawaf al-ifadah. People who live in Makkah do not owe it either.

"…no sexual relations… during Hajj." Before Arafah it spoils the Hajj in all four schools — the Hajj is still completed and then repeated another year; after Arafah the schools differ. Every other violation is repaired by a fidyah, or by nothing.
"…nothing except Paradise." Mabrur: done sincerely, the Sunnah way, without sin — and a life that changes after it.

"…perform tawaf of the Ka'bah and between Safa and Marwah, then cut short his hair and finish his ihram, and later assume ihram for Hajj." Many scholars advise a trim when the {1}th is near, so there is hair to shave on the Day of Nahr.

"…than these ten days." They asked: "Not even jihad in the path of Allah?" He said: "Not even jihad, except a man who goes out with himself and his wealth and returns with nothing." Your Hajj sits inside the best days of the year.
"…the day of Arafah. He draws near, then praises them before the angels: What do these want?" Bring your dua list — and your family's.
"…the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men… or an expiation: feeding needy people, or the equivalent of that in fasting."

A man in a perfumed cloak was simply told to take it off and wash off the scent. Forgetting is not a sin; whether a fidyah is still owed differs — Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse clothing and perfume, Hanafis and Malikis do not.
After Hajar's seventh run between Safa and Marwah, an angel struck the ground with his heel (or wing) at the place of Zamzam, near where baby Isma'il lay, and the water gushed out (Bukhari {1}).

Aishah (RA) perfumed him "for his release, when he came out of ihram, before he performed tawaf" — that is, before tawaf al-ifadah. Clothes, nails and perfume return at this first release; intimacy waits for tawaf al-ifadah — and, for most schools, the sa'i too if you still owe it. (Malikis also keep hunting forbidden and dislike perfume until then; Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis keep the marriage contract forbidden.)
Aishah (RA): Quraysh (al-Hums) stayed at Muzdalifah while the other Arabs stood at Arafah; with Islam, Allah ordered His Prophet ﷺ to go to Arafah, stand there and depart from there.

Aishah (RA): those who had done Umrah first "performed another tawaf (between Safa and Marwah) after returning from Mina." The four schools require this second sa'i of the Tamattu' pilgrim, normally after tawaf al-ifadah; a minority (e.g. Ibn Taymiyyah) held the first sa'i suffices.
Ajwa dates of Madinah (Bukhari {1}) — the perfect gift to bring home.
Al-Abbas (RA) asked to stay in Makkah for the siqayah and was allowed; the herders were allowed to stay with the camels and gather their stoning. Scholars extend this to others with a real need.
All four schools allow the one unable to delegate the stoning; the deputy normally throws his own pebbles first. Malikis add that the one unable still owes a dam.
Anas (RA) heard the Prophet ﷺ say "Labbayka 'umratan wa hajjan." Tamattu' says "'Umrah"; Ifrad says "Hajjan"; "'an …" is said only when performing for someone else.
Anas (RA): he came to the Jamrah and stoned it, went to his place in Mina and sacrificed, then called the barber — and then rode to the House. Ifrad has no hady: stone, cut, tawaf.
Asked what the muhrim wears, the Prophet ﷺ said: "He should not wear a shirt, a turban, trousers, a hooded cloak or leather socks" — nor clothes scented with saffron or wars.

Badal is established: "Labbayk on behalf of Shubrumah…" — the Prophet ﷺ said to perform your own (Hajj) first, then his (Abu Dawud {1}). Shafi'is and Hanbalis make this a condition; Hanafis and Malikis hold a proxy pilgrimage before your own is valid but disliked — doing your own first is the safe course.
Bukhari {1} — a thousand-fold, exceeded only by Masjid al-Haram.
Bukhari {1} — and the accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise.
Bukhari {1} — at its foot rest Hamza (RA) and the seventy martyrs of Uhud.
Dhul-Hulayfah, just outside Madinah — the farthest miqat from Makkah (~{1} km).
Dhul-Hulayfah, just outside Madinah — the miqat the Prophet ﷺ set for the people of Madinah, and the one he used for his own Hajj.
Every tribe lifted a corner of the cloth, and al-Amin ﷺ set the Stone in place with his own hands.
Face the Black Stone, say "Bismillahi wallahu akbar", then keep the Kaaba on your left.

False — "Our Lord, do not hold us to account for what we forget or err in" (Quran {1}). There is no sin — learn, correct, continue. But most schools still require a fidyah for some slips (e.g. shaving or clipping nails), and most hold intercourse invalidates it even if forgotten — ask a scholar.
False — "Tawaf around the House is like salah, except that you speak in it; so whoever speaks, let him speak only good." (Tirmidhi {1})
False — "There are angels at the entrances of Madinah: neither plague nor the Dajjal can enter it." (Bukhari {1})
False — "all of Arafat is a place of standing" (Ibn Majah {1}); only the hollow of Uranah lies outside it. Sitting in the tent counts in full.
False — "except the menstruating women, who were excused" (Bukhari {1}). Tawaf al-ifadah, however, must still be done once she is pure.
False — Jeddah lies inside the miqat boundaries for most routes, so ihram must be assumed before the plane crosses the miqat.
False — beloved and highly virtuous (one of the three mosques worth travelling to — Bukhari {1}), but not part of the rites of Umrah or Hajj, and it needs no ihram.
False — both are sunnah for men in the arrival tawaf (Hanafis and Shafi'is: also in a later tawaf followed by sa'i); leaving them affects nothing.
False — no dua is prescribed per round. Only "Rabbana atina…" between the Yamani corner and Black Stone is sunnah.

False — tawaf al-ifadah is a pillar. "Would she delay us?" he asked about Safiyyah, until told she had already done it. She waits until she is pure; if her travel truly cannot wait, she asks a scholar before leaving. Only the farewell is waived.
False — the light jog there is for men; women walk throughout.
False — the opposite: the niqab is specifically not worn in ihram, and in the majority view gloves are not either (Bukhari {1}). Ordinary modest dress applies.
False — the requirement is an izar and rida not tailored to the body (a hem or seam is fine); clean is expected, white is recommended, and new is not required. Spares and washing are fine.
False — they first faced Jerusalem; the qibla changed mid-prayer (~{1} AH) — Quran {2}, commemorated at Masjid al-Qiblatayn.

For the majority, the talbiyah continues from the miqat until you start your tawaf. Malikis stop it on entering the Haram (or, if ihram was from Tan'eem, on seeing the Kaaba) — if that is your school, your practice is sound.
Four: Hudaybiyyah, al-Qada, al-Ji'ranah, and the one with his Hajj (Bukhari {1}, {2}).
Fully valid — the Prophet ﷺ himself performed tawaf mounted (Bukhari {1}).
Gesture from afar with "Allahu Akbar" and continue — harming others for a sunnah is never right.
Glasses, watches, rings, umbrellas and sandals are all fine in ihram.
He stayed nine years in Madinah without performing Hajj, then announced it in the tenth year — his only Hajj after the Hijrah.

He ﷺ "kept reciting the talbiyah till he did the rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah" (Bukhari {1}). Some continue to the last pebble. Malikis stop it on arriving at Arafah after midday on the {2}th — if that is your school, your practice is sound.

He ﷺ "kept reciting the talbiyah till he did the rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah." Stopping at tawaf is the rule of Umrah, not Hajj. Some stop at the last pebble; Malikis stop on reaching Arafah after midday on the {1}th — if that is your school, your practice is sound.
His two closest companions and successors — greet all three with a calm salam.
